### Selected projects

**Travel Atlas: Validated Data Pipeline, SQL Edit Checks, and Interactive Map**\
*Independent project*, 10/2026 – present ([live site](https://ziang-atlas.pages.dev) | [GitHub](https://github.com/Markholmezza/travel-atlas))

* Directed AI-assisted development (Claude Code) of a Leaflet map of 49 places in 19 countries, with Python pipelines that turn flight logs, GPS tracks, and Word/PDF articles into CSV and GeoJSON, deployed through Cloudflare Pages.
* Wrote a 55-rule data validation plan modeled on clinical edit checks, each with an ID, severity, rationale, and revision history, and enforced it in Python file checks, SQLite constraints, and SQL cross-record queries with recursive CTEs.
* Gated deployment on validation: any error fails the Cloudflare Pages build so nothing is published; 103 automated tests cover one deliberately broken dataset per rule, and the checks caught 7 flight records that violated the data dictionary.

**Coronary Heart Disease Risk Model: Data Audit and Survey-Weighted Revalidation (NHANES)**\
*Independent project based on an Emory project*, 09/2025 – present ([GitHub](https://github.com/Markholmezza/nhanes-chd) | [Shiny app](shiny.html))

* Found that a one-to-many join on participant ID turned 5,751 NHANES adults into 15,103 rows, leaking 75% of test rows into training; fixing the pipeline cut random-forest AUC from 0.999 to 0.86, matching a plain logistic regression.
* Built a three-page interactive Power BI report covering 20,469 adults in three NHANES cycles, with DAX measures for survey-weighted prevalence and a what-if threshold slider that updates the sensitivity, specificity, and the share flagged.
* Framed the model for care-management outreach: contacting the riskiest 10% of adults would reach 50% of CHD cases (5.0 times the random rate) and contacting 30% would reach 86%, with the capacity trade-offs shown per 10,000 adults.
* Evaluated models along TRIPOD with bootstrap CIs, calibration, and decision curves; the paper's PSO-ANN reached AUC 0.836, significantly below logistic regression (0.859), and class weighting inflated the mean predicted risk sevenfold.
* Double-programmed the 2013–2014 survey-weighted prevalence and complete-case odds ratios in Python and R (`survey`), matching to within 0.0005; documented the data lineage, methods, and limitations in a reproducible GitHub repository.

**Blocked Dose-Response Field Experiment: Predator Odor and Squirrel Foraging (Time-to-Event)**\
*Emory University project*, 09/2025 – 12/2025 ([GitHub](https://github.com/Markholmezza/squirrel-foraging-survival-analysis))

* Designed a blocked dose-response field experiment after a pilot study (4 blocks × 4 urine doses, 160 walnuts, 10 checks over 123 hours); modeled the right-censored removal times with Kaplan–Meier curves and adjusted log-rank tests in R.
* Added a post hoc block-stratified Cox model with station-clustered SEs: the removal hazard at the 100% dose was 0.15 (95% CI 0.07–0.32) of control, with a trend hazard ratio of 0.56 per dose step and no violation of proportional hazards.
